next_step: Run 2-week POC: ingest ~6M docs, validate 200-500 QPS with embed+rerank, measure cost/QPS and p99 latency
notes:
Context: mid-market SaaS that provides knowledge-base search for multiple enterprise customers (Zendesk + SFDC + GDrive connectors). Wants hosted API but strict SSO/SOC2 for enterprise tenants.

Recent activity:
- 2026-02-14 discovery call (Maya, Liam) w/ VP Eng (Carlos D.) + Product PM (Hannah). Carlos: "Need sub-200ms end-to-end for top-k rerank at 200 QPS baseline; peak up to 500 QPS for support spikes."
- 2026-02-28 architecture deep-dive; SE asked for expected index size: team estimates 5-8M docs (long-form KB pages + attachments), avg doc length ~1.2k tokens.
- 2026-03-02 security kickoff w/ security ops (audit reqs, SSO info). Provided SOC2 cert and ID token flow questions.
- 2026-03-08 commercial call; pricing sensitivity noted: target cost/query $0.005-$0.02 when amortized over retrieval+rerank.

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria (customer):
- Ingestion: 5–8M docs, connectors for Zendesk + SFDC + Drive, dedupe & chunking strategy required.
- Retrieval: vector store w/ ANN (approx) for high QPS; warm cache recommended.
- Reranking: two-stage pipeline (fast candidate recall using 1536-d embeddings, followed by 3B reranker for top-10). p99 rerank latency target <150–200ms.
- SLA targets: 99.5% availability, <200ms median retrieval, <300ms 95th for rerank under steady 200 QPS.
- Cost control: prefer batching, quantized models, prioritized routing to cheaper model variants during non-peak.
- Security: SSO (SAML), audit logs for queries, per-tenant isolation (logical), at-rest encryption.

POC plan (agreed):
- Week 0: access + account setup (hosted API trial) + sample index (200k docs) to validate pipeline.
- Week 1: full ingest run for 2M docs, run load tests at 100/200 QPS, gather latencies and token costs.
- Week 2: scale to 6M docs, A/B reranker (local vs Redwood hosted reranker), evaluate quality (MRR) and cost/Q.
- Deliverable: performance deck + cost breakdown + recommendation.

Quotes / snippets: "We care about deterministic economics — show us cost per effective query, not just model price." — Product PM.

Open risks / Concerns captured:
- Long documents + chunking strategy may blow up candidate set -> increased rerank cost.
- Data residency: some enterprise tenants require EU residency; currently Meridian expects Redwood to clarify region placement.
- Legal needs standard SLA + right to audit clause.

Quick wins suggested by SE:
- Enable prefix/KV caching on popular queries, 2x reduction in rerank calls for support macros.
- Use lower-dim embeddings for ANN stage (cost savings) and keep higher-cap reranker for top-k.

Sales notes (short):
- Champion: Carlos Dominguez (VP Eng) — cares about latency, predictable cost.
- Economic buyer: CFO (involved for mid-size deployments).
- Timeline: procurement target Q2 2026 if POC OK.
- Decision factors: latency under load, predictable unit econ, SOC2 + SSO fit, connector maturity.

Next actions (owner):
- Maya to spin up POC account, share ingestion checklist (by 2026-03-12).
- Liam to propose batching/quantization config + example cost model (by 2026-03-15).
- Legal to provide standard MSA + SLA template (requested 2026-03-09).
summary: Meridian Lattice Search is running an evaluation for hosted Redwood API focused on embeddings + reranking for a KB RAG product. Moderate index scale (5–8M docs), high QPS (200–500), needs sub-200ms rerank p99 and clear cost/Q metrics. POC scheduled for Mar 2026; blockers are budget and data-residency/legal clarifications.
